cards.text: David wrote this song for the choirmaster back when he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah. The heading says Joab, commander of David's army (2 Samuel 8:16), came back and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. So you'd expect a victory party, right? HOLD ON to your apron, friend.

cards.question: David opens his song talking straight to God. What does David say God has done to His people?

cards.text: You've rejected us, You've broken us, You've been angry. David does NOT tiptoe, and then he finishes the line with one big ask: 'restore us!'

cards.question: David keeps going with a picture. What does he say God has done to the land?

answers.text: Shaken it and torn it open
Dried it out with no rain

cards.question: The land is quaking, so David asks God to ___ its fractures.
Next, David tells God that His people have had nothing but easy days. True or false?

cards.text: David says God has shown His people hardship, and they're staggered from the wine He made them drink. I know staggering, friend: my first hop on this gold base after years lying flat in a drawer, I wobbled across the bakery like a stack of cookies on a SPIN CYCLE.
Then the song turns. David points to something God has done for those who fear Him.

cards.question: For those who fear Him, what has God raised?
God has raised a banner for those who fear Him. What's it there for?

answers.text: So they can flee the bow
So they can mark the border
So they can count the troops

cards.text: Then comes 'Selah,' and GOOD, because I needed a breather after all that. When the song picks back up, David asks God to respond and save them with His right hand.

cards.question: David asks God to save them with His right hand, so that His beloved may be ___.

cards.text: Now David brings in God's own words. God has spoken from His sanctuary, and friend, when GOD speaks, the whole bakery goes quiet. Even the ovens.

cards.question: David has been praying about rejection and hardship. Then come God's words from His sanctuary. How do they open?

cards.text: God says, 'I will triumph!' Then He calls out places across the land like a roll call: Shechem, the Valley of Succoth, Gilead, Manasseh.

cards.question: God says He'll parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth. What's He showing about this land?

answers.text: It's too far gone to save

cards.question: God calls Ephraim His helmet, and Judah His ___.

cards.text: Then God turns to the nations nearby, and Moab, He says, is His washbasin. Not His crown, not His throne, His WASHBASIN.

cards.question: Next comes Edom. What does God say He tosses upon Edom?
Over Philistia, God says He'll weep in sorrow. True or false?

cards.text: Over Philistia, God shouts in triumph. That's the end of God's words, and now David's back with a question of his own.

cards.question: David asks, 'Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to ___?'

cards.text: Then David asks, 'Have You not rejected us, O God?' There's that word again, friend: rejected.

cards.question: In that same breath, David asks if God will no longer do something with their armies. What is it?

cards.text: So David asks God for aid against the enemy. And he says exactly why it has to come from God.

cards.question: Why does David say the aid against the enemy has to come from God?

answers.text: The help of man is worthless

cards.text: Worthless, he says, and I get it: back in my worn-down days, Mother Miller pressed me harder and harder and STILL got blurry cookies. Now David sings the last line of the song.

cards.question: In the last line of the song, David says God will trample their enemies. True or false?

cards.text: And there it is: 'With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.' The fight's still out there, but David knows who he's going in with, and friend, that changes EVERYTHING.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: the song's occasion, Joab's victory, 'So you'd expect a victory party, right?', and 'HOLD ON to your apron, friend.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Card 1 says 'you'd expect a victory party' and then 'HOLD ON.' That tells the baker the answer is something negative. Both wrong answers ('Lifted them high', 'Made them rich') are positive, so the setup rules them out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'widen' and 'hide' don't make sense. David has just begged 'restore us!' and says the land is quaking, so no baker would believe he asks God to widen or hide its fractures. That leaves 'heal' as the only real choice.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke blends two images: Papa Dorin wobbling on his base, and 'a stack of cookies on a SPIN CYCLE.' Cookies in a washing machine's spin cycle doesn't click right away, so a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Card 8 only says 'David points to something God has done.' The baker then has to guess a detail (banner, altar or tower) with nothing to reason from. This is the same kind of question as the Psalm 23 bad example (oil, myrrh or perfume).

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: Card 11 has just told the baker that David asks God to 'save them.' That gives away 'delivered,' which means nearly the same thing, and it rules out 'scattered' and 'forgotten,' which are the opposite of being saved.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer calls God's opening words 'a shout of triumph.' Psalm 60:6 says 'I will triumph!' The word 'shout' belongs to verse 8 ('over Philistia I shout in triumph'), and card 9 uses it there too. The answer swaps in wording from a different verse.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the next word of a line ('Judah is My ___': scepter, shield or sword). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out. It tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess a detail (sandal, cloak or staff) with no context to reason from. Like the Psalm 23 bad example, it tests a detail instead of the picture or its meaning.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: 'So David asks God for aid' adds a cause-and-effect link between verse 10 and verse 11 that the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to his 'worn-down days' and Mother Miller pressing harder and still getting blurry cookies. Nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up, and onboarding only establishes the junk drawer. The line also makes Mother Miller's effort stand in for the 'worthless' help of man, which doesn't fit his kind, grudge-free character.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: Most cards carry no humor at all, for example stop 1 cards 3 and 8, and stop 2 cards 3, 9, 11 and 13. The few jokes are mild or don't land, so the walkthrough reads like a pleasant narrator rather than laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
